``` Created At: 2026-06-19T11:24:08Z Completed At: 2026-06-19T11:24:11Z The search for "broot unlisted ellipsis" returned the following summary: In **broot**, the "unlisted" ellipsis (`...`) appears at the bottom of a directory listing to indicate that the folder contains more files than are currently being displayed[1][2]. This is a core feature designed to keep the interface clean and focused on an "overview" of the file system rather than dumping massive lists of files[2][3].
### Key Details * **Why it appears:** Broot defaults to a truncated view to ensure the UI remains fast and readable[2][3]. Instead of scrolling through long lists, you are encouraged to use fuzzy search (just start typing) to find the specific file or directory you need[2][3]. * **How to show everything:** If you need to see all files in a directory, you can toggle the full listing by using the `:toggle_trim_root` verb (or simply typing `:t` in the command prompt)[4][3]. * **Styling:** You can customize the appearance of the ellipsis in your `conf.toml` (or `.hjson`) configuration file under the `[skin]` section using the `purpose_ellipsis` setting[5]. * **Persistent behavior:** If you prefer to always see full listings by default, you can launch broot with the flag `broot --cmd ":t"` or define this as a default command in your configuration, though this is generally discouraged as it deviates from the intended design of the tool[3].

``` Created At: 2026-06-19T11:24:14Z Completed At: 2026-06-19T11:24:17Z The search for "broot ellipsis at end of folder name" returned the following summary: In **broot**, an ellipsis (`…`) at the end of a folder name (or filename) indicates that the name has been **truncated** because it is too long to fit within the available column width of your terminal window[1][2].
This is standard behavior in many terminal-based file managers and UI components to ensure that the interface remains readable and that columns stay aligned when filenames exceed the space allocated to them[3][4].
### Why this happens * **Space Constraints:** When your terminal window is narrow or the column for filenames is limited by other displayed information (like file size, permissions, or dates), `broot` truncates the text to prevent it from overlapping or breaking the layout[3][5]. * **Visual Indicator:** The ellipsis acts as a visual cue to let you know that the full name is longer than what is currently being displayed[2].
### How to see the full name If you need to see the full, untruncated name, you can usually try the following: * **Resize your terminal:** Widening your terminal window will often give `broot` enough space to display the full filename[3]. * **Adjust column visibility:** If you are displaying extra information (like dates or sizes), you can try toggling those off to give the filename column more room[5][6]. * **Navigate into the folder:** If you move into the directory, the path or file list may be reformatted in a way that provides more space for the names.

## Assistant
Both elements in your `broot` screenshot are visual tools for keeping the file tree compact and clean:
### 1. **"N unlisted"** Because `broot` is designed to dynamically fit your entire directory tree on a single terminal screen without scrolling, it hides less relevant files based on its sizing heuristics. * **"N unlisted"** means there are $N$ files/directories inside that folder that aren't being displayed right now to save vertical space. * **To see everything:** You can press `:t` (or `:toggle_trim_root`) to toggle showing all files in the current view. Alternatively, just type a search term, and `broot` will automatically uncover the unlisted files if they match your query.
### 2. **The `...` (Ellipsis) on names** An ellipsis at the end of a directory or file name (like `meetings/26-06-07-first-meeting-hello ...` or `agent ...`) means **the text is truncated** because it is too long to fit in the current horizontal space. * **Why it happens:** Either the filename itself is very long, or the terminal window/column width is constrained. * **To see the full name:** You can widen your terminal window, toggle off extra columns (like sizes/dates if you have them enabled), or select/focus the item to view its details.
